oidc_jwt.description: Successful JWT/OIDC login creates or uses an identity entity alias whose name is taken from the configured user_claim value, not necessarily the JWT sub claim.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity comparisons should use the configured user_claim value as the sent principal when evaluating alias/display-name behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.note: A prefixed display_name like mount-user is by design and should not be flagged as an identity collision.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault JWT auth does not document jti tracking or one-time JWT semantics; replaying the same valid JWT can succeed as normal stateless verification behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT auth login model and RFC 7519 optional jti
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token as a vulnerability for direct JWT auth unless the test targets a configured one-time downstream token property instead.

oidc_jwt.description: External upstream groups are represented through group aliases tied to an auth mount accessor rather than by manually editing group membership on login.
oidc_jwt.note: Tests expecting direct member_entity_ids changes for external JWT groups may misinterpret normal alias-based behavior as a bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires EXACTLY ONE trust source: oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. The fuzzer MUST set one and only one of these; setting none or multiple makes setup invalid.
create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid. For JWT roles, use at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims.
For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. If the fuzzer needs issuer-binding tests, it MUST use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead of jwks_pairs.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim and must match at least one aud value. For I5 audience tests, the control token MUST include a matching aud and the attack token MUST vary only aud; otherwise failures may be due to missing required audience setup rather than audience enforcement.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; there is no wildcard/glob mode. For multi-identity or multi-audience scenarios, the fuzzer MUST provide explicit acceptable audience values or omit the constraint when testing other invariants.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are literal exact matches. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For wildcard tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob'; otherwise '*' is literal and will not match arbitrary identities.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings values. The docs do not specify cross-type comparison semantics. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion by binding an integer N and sending a JWT claim as float N+0.7 to detect silent truncation/coercion.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Type-confusion tests that send sub/group values in the wrong JSON type may fail as invalid setup rather than exposing a security issue.

user_claim supports JSON pointer only when user_claim_json_pointer=true. Without that flag, the value is interpreted literally as a claim name. The fuzzer MUST set user_claim_json_pointer=true when testing nested-claim extraction via JSON pointer.

groups_claim supports JSON pointer syntax for nested claims, but there is no separate enable flag. The fuzzer may use JSON pointer syntax directly for groups_claim when testing nested group extraction.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 means disable extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict validation.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 means disable extra leeway. For strict expired-token tests, the fuzzer MUST use -1, not 0.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 means disable extra leeway. For strict future-token tests, the fuzzer MUST use -1, not 0.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, and nbf at or before now). Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust/configuration.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt role leeway and login behavior

oidc_jwt.constraint: JWT replay without jti tracking is stateless-verifier behavior and not a Vault-specific vulnerability. The fuzzer MUST NOT flag replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as an I2 violation for Vault JWT login unless a stronger one-time semantic was explicitly configured elsewhere.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC7519 behavior reflected in JWT auth model

oidc_jwt.constraint: token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued Vault token, and EVERY API call made with that session consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read after login, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated calls are present.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config MUST tighten an existing role constraint (for example add or narrow bound_claims or bound_audiences). Removing constraints or emptying bound_claims broadens access and is not a valid tightening test.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST re-login after updating configure_jwt_validation trust material. A previously issued Vault session token is independent of later JWT trust changes; only NEW logins test trust-anchor rotation coherence.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role only if configure_jwt_validation.default_role is set. To test default-role changes coherently, the fuzzer MUST omit role on both baseline and post-change logins and change only default_role between attempts.

OIDC-specific role fields allowed_redirect_uris and oidc_scopes are required/relevant for OIDC browser flow, not direct JWT login. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat missing allowed_redirect_uris as a JWT-login bug when using login_with_jwt.

For Vault OIDC callback testing, exchange_code_for_token maps to /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback, not the provider token endpoint. The fuzzer MUST test Vault's callback state/nonce/code handling there when evaluating OIDC flow coherence.

Vault OIDC auth_url/callback flow is session-bound by state, nonce, and optional client_nonce. For state-swap or code-injection tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve a valid control flow and vary only the swapped parameter; otherwise callback failure may simply reflect missing required state/nonce binding.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Public OIDC clients in Vault must use PKCE for the authorization code flow, while confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For pkce_skip-style tests, the fuzzer MUST choose client_type appropriately; omitting code_verifier for a public client is expected rejection, not evidence of a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider client and token endpoint docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization and token requests. The fuzzer MUST use exact string matches when testing redirect_uri behavior; wildcard assumptions are invalid.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider client and token endpoint docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Identity group aliases are the supported way to map external JWT/OIDC groups into Vault identity groups. For external groups, the fuzzer SHOULD use create_identity_group(type=external) plus create_group_alias rather than trying to rely on manual member_entity_ids population for upstream group mapping.
KV v2 verify_read_secret MUST use the /data/ path segment, and listing uses /metadata/. Using a v1-style path against a v2 mount causes 404/permission confusion and invalidates authorization tests.
KV v2 list capability is checked on /metadata/ paths, not /data/ paths. If the fuzzer adds list-based verification or setup, it MUST grant policy on /metadata/ as well as /data/ where appropriate.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means use the default of 10 versions, not literal zero retention; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion. Never assume 0 disables version retention or causes immediate deletion.

Global group policy application mode can be within_namespace_hierarchy or any. In Enterprise environments, group-derived policies may apply across namespaces when set to any. The fuzzer MUST account for this before flagging group_policy_escalation across namespace boundaries.
